You were with someone for four years, and at a young age when people are still figuring out what kind of person they are. Regardless of the bad ending, it's going to take some time to get over the whole situation.

I went through something similar a few years ago. At 19 years old, got my first girlfriend; things were going well at first, and we were living together about 6 months into the relationship (both in college). Around the 14 month mark, breakup happens - her cheating on me with an ex. Became a real cunt towards me, flip-flopping between stringing me along and being cold. She ended up marrying the ex - someone she she had brought up on rape charges in the past - about 6 months after our breakup.

Through all of the shit, it probably took me a solid 18 months to really be over her. Even after all the anger I felt towards her, especially after finding out she married the guy, I still had remaining feelings and hated myself for it. I ended up in some very dark places mentally, and it took time and some therapy to get out of that mindset.

But looking back on it, her dumping me was, hands down, one of the best things to happen to me in my life. I wouldn't have broken up with her, even though the relationship was obviously (in retrospect) going down the tubes. And most importantly, I learned so much about myself from the failed relationship. I wasn't close to being a perfect boyfriend, and I saw what parts about myself I could improve and fix. I learned what my hard-lined "No's" were in regards to potential partners, and the experience taught me how to prepare myself for future relationships so a potential breakup isn't so emotionally devastating.

It's okay that you're still having residual feelings. The emotional wounds from the relationship are still healing, and will be for some time. But they will heal, and when the emotions are gone, you'll look back and cringe at yourself for dating him in the first place. And don't stress about some of the mistakes you made in the relationship. We all make those mistakes, especially at such young ages. Take from those mistakes and learn from them, so that in your next relationship you can be better for both yourself and your partner.

Time will be the main factor in feeling better, but for the time being occupy yourself with schoolwork and friends/classmates. Do things that make you happy, and your mind from wandering. On the same note, when your mind does start to wander towards him, use anger to your advantage. It helps in keeping desire to be back with them at bay.

To end on a lighter note - my ex, who had slowly crept up to being a bit overweight by the end of the relationship, ballooned into a full dependapotamus since getting married.
